title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named campus spaces documented by Syracuse University for quiet work, group projects, conversation, and student events.

cards.title: Safire Room
cards.subtitle: Sixth floor, Bird Library
cards.notes: Bring reading or a laptop to the sixth floor and use the quiet-work room’s campus view for a focused session between classes.
cards.short_summary: A book-lined Bird Library room for quiet work with a panoramic campus view.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies the Safire Room on Bird Library’s sixth floor as a space for quiet work and notes its panoramic campus view.
cards.access_notes: Located in Bird Library; the library reports public access until 7 p.m. on regular business days, with extended access requiring valid SU or SUNY-ESF ID.

cards.title: Carnegie Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Carnegie Library, Shaw Quadrangle
cards.notes: Choose a table in the historic reading room when you want a dedicated quiet-study setting rather than a group lounge.
cards.short_summary: A historic, naturally lit reading room for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University describes Carnegie Library’s historic Reading Room as a quiet-study space with high ceilings, arches, and a domed skylight.
cards.access_notes: The University locates Carnegie Library on the Shaw Quadrangle and lists team rooms, workstations, and a printer room in the building.

cards.title: Noble Room
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Hendricks Chapel
cards.notes: Use the couches and chairs to compare notes with classmates; the nearby People’s Place Café is optional if you want food or coffee.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level Hendricks Chapel setting for relaxed group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University states that the Noble Room, on Hendricks Chapel’s lower level, offers couches and chairs for comparing notes with classmates.
cards.source_title: Ten Great Places to Study for Finals
cards.access_notes: Inside Hendricks Chapel. The chapel lists academic-year building hours of 8 a.m.–9 p.m.; confirm access around events and breaks.

cards.title: Panasci Lounge
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Schine Student Center
cards.notes: Set up at a lounge seat facing Hall of Languages when you need a quieter place to read, write, or work between activities.
cards.short_summary: A glass-filled Schine lounge with seating oriented toward Hall of Languages.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University describes Panasci Lounge as a glass-filled second-floor space in Schine Student Center facing Hall of Languages and used for assignments.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Schine Student Center; the University describes its seating as suitable for studying, group meetings, or lounging.

cards.title: The Underground
cards.subtitle: Bottom floor, Schine Student Center
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the lounge or check the campus calendar for a lecture, concert, meeting, or other scheduled event in the adjacent venue.
cards.short_summary: A Schine lower-level lounge and event venue used for campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says The Underground is on Schine Student Center’s bottom floor and that its venue is used for meetings, banquets, lectures, and concerts.
cards.access_notes: Inside Schine Student Center; event access and seating availability depend on scheduled programming.

cards.title: Mower Passage
cards.subtitle: Connecting Newhouse 1 and Newhouse 2
cards.notes: Use this indoor passage’s padded chairs and daylight for a brief reading session or a waiting spot between Newhouse classes.
cards.short_summary: A sunlit Newhouse connector with lounge seating and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies Mower Passage as the connection between Newhouse 1 and 2 and describes its padded chairs and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.access_notes: An interior connector between Newhouse 1 and Newhouse 2; access can vary with building schedules.

cards.title: Link Hall
cards.subtitle: College of Engineering and Computer Science building
cards.notes: Head to a walk-in lounge or the top-floor hallway when you need a place to read, wait, or work while looking across Shaw Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: Engineering building with walk-in lounges and a top-floor view over Shaw Quadrangle.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University reports that Link Hall has walk-in graduate and undergraduate lounges and a top-floor hallway overlooking Shaw Quadrangle.
cards.access_notes: Most of Link Hall is used by the College of Engineering and Computer Science; use normal building access and posted policies.

cards.title: Gerry's Café
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Eggers Hall
cards.notes: Use the glass-lined seating as a daytime stop for individual work or a conversation; food is optional and service details can change.
cards.short_summary: An Eggers Hall café seating area adjacent to Maxwell Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University places Gerry’s Café on Eggers Hall’s third floor, adjacent to Maxwell Hall, and describes its glass-lined eatery and seating.
cards.access_notes: Inside Eggers Hall; the cited University story says food service was Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–3 p.m., while building access is separate.

cards.title: Hinds ICE Box
cards.subtitle: School of Information Studies
cards.notes: Bring a project team to the Innovation, Collaboration and Entrepreneurship Center for a work session or to develop an early-stage idea.
cards.short_summary: An iSchool space for project work, collaboration, and entrepreneurship.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says the Hinds ICE Box is the Innovation, Collaboration and Entrepreneurship Center for students working on projects or startup companies.
cards.source_title: Ten Great Places to Study for Finals
cards.access_notes: Located in the School of Information Studies; confirm availability and any reservation requirements with the school.

cards.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Library
cards.subtitle: Sims Hall
cards.notes: Work near the computer cluster or media workstation, then take time to look at the library’s rare and first-edition collections.
cards.short_summary: A Sims Hall library combining study technology with art and rare-book collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University locates the Martin Luther King Jr. Library in Sims Hall and notes its rare and first-edition collections, computer cluster, and media workstation.
cards.source_title: Ten Great Places to Study for Finals
cards.access_notes: Located in Sims Hall; check College of Arts and Sciences or building information for current access details.
